nodes.name: Aerospace carbon-fiber composite material (fairings & structures)
nodes.description: Aerospace-grade PAN-based carbon fiber plus matrix resin / prepreg used to build payload fairings and other composite primary structures on reusable launch vehicles. On Falcon 9 the payload fairing is a carbon fiber-aluminum honeycomb sandwich. Fairing FABRICATION is substantially captive at SpaceX (its own Hawthorne autoclaves); the MERCHANT exposure is the upstream carbon-fiber + resin material tier (Toray, Hexcel, Teijin, Mitsubishi Chemical, Syensqo). High-modulus / high-strength aerospace carbon fiber sits under a standing export-control regime (Wassenaar dual-use list; U.S. EAR/ITAR), a structural constraint on who may supply and to whom.
nodes.notes: Merchant tier = carbon-fiber + resin material; fairing lay-up/cure is captive at SpaceX. Single-/near-single-source character lives in aerospace-QUALIFIED intermediate-modulus tow, where a handful of producers (Toray, Hexcel, Teijin, Mitsubishi Chemical) are qualified into flight programs and Toray controls >50% of upstream PAN precursor. Export-control regime (Wassenaar/EAR) is a standing constraint, not a dated episode.

nodes.name: Composite-overwrapped pressure vessel (COPV) for helium pressurant
nodes.description: Composite-overwrapped pressure vessel storing high-pressure helium used to pressurize a launch vehicle's propellant tanks as engines consume propellant. Industry-standard construction is carbon-fiber composite overwrapped over a thin metal (e.g. aluminum) liner; newer Type IV/Type V designs use polymer-lined or linerless carbon overwrap. On Falcon 9 the COPVs sit inside the propellant tanks and SpaceX BUILDS ITS OWN COPVs (captive). The merchant population — Infinite Composites, Steelhead Composites, HyPerComp, General Dynamics-OTS — supplies COPVs to the broader launch / spacecraft industry and is the investable exposure for non-captive programs; the carbon-fiber overwrap itself ties back to the same aerospace carbon-fiber material tier.
nodes.notes: CAPTIVE at SpaceX (builds its own COPVs). Merchant COPV makers exist for the wider industry (Infinite Composites, Steelhead, HyPerComp, GD-OTS) and are mapped as reported_capable_supplier, not as SpaceX's manufacturer. Single-source history: the CRS-7 (2015) and AMOS-6 (2016) Falcon 9 losses both traced to COPV behavior, underscoring the qualification difficulty of this part.

nodes.name: Toray Industries
nodes.description: Japanese chemicals/materials group; the world's largest carbon fiber producer (TORAYCA brand; owns Zoltek for large-tow industrial fiber). Supplies aerospace-grade intermediate-/high-modulus carbon fiber used in commercial-aircraft primary structures and, as a material tier, in launch-vehicle composite structures (fairings) and COPV overwrap. Also dominant in the upstream PAN precursor that nearly all carbon fiber requires.

metrics.name: Global carbon fiber capacity
metrics.description: CompositesWorld: Toray has 'a capacity to produce almost 58,000 tons of regular tow and large tow carbon fiber' across plants in Japan, France, Korea, Hungary, Mexico and the U.S. Total-company tow capacity basis (regular + large tow, not aerospace-only).

metrics.name: Global PAN precursor share
metrics.description: CompositesWorld: Toray 'reportedly controls more than 50% of the global polyacrylonitrile (PAN) fiber market'; PAN is the precursor for >2 lb per 1 lb of carbon fiber. Qualitative '>50%' floor, precursor-market basis.

nodes.notes: World's largest carbon fiber producer; merchant material tier feeding fairing/structure lay-up and COPV overwrap. Ticker 3402.T (Tokyo) verified this round via exchange listing. Aerospace qualification + Wassenaar/EAR export control narrow who can ship high-modulus tow.

nodes.name: Hexcel Corporation
nodes.description: U.S. advanced-composites maker (NYSE: HXL); HexTow carbon fiber and HexPly prepreg are primary-structure materials on major commercial and military aircraft (A350 XWB, Boeing 787, JSF). Intermediate-modulus fiber leader with in-house PAN precursor. As a material tier it feeds launch-vehicle composite structures and, via HexTow IM-grade fiber, COPV overwrap (e.g. a Type IV COPV co-developed with HyPerComp).

metrics.name: 2024 net sales to Airbus + subcontractors
metrics.description: Hexcel 2024 Form 10-K (per filing text): ~40% of 2024 net sales were to Airbus and its subcontractors (37% Commercial Aerospace, 3% Space & Defense). Customer-concentration basis. NOTE: primary 10-K PDF/HTML did not render readable text to this agent; figure corroborated across multiple secondary reports of the 10-K — treat as paywalled_snippet pending owner re-fetch.

metrics.description: Hexcel 2024 Form 10-K (per filing text): ~15% of 2024 net sales were to Boeing and its subcontractors (13% Commercial Aerospace, 2% Space & Defense). Customer-concentration basis. Same fetch caveat as the Airbus figure.

nodes.notes: Merchant carbon-fiber + prepreg tier; also a COPV-relevant fiber supplier (HexTow IM11-R in a Type IV COPV with HyPerComp). Ticker HXL (NYSE) verified this round. Customer-concentration percentages flagged paywalled_snippet: the 10-K primary text was not machine-readable to this agent.

nodes.name: Teijin
nodes.description: Japanese materials group (Tokyo: 3401); Teijin Carbon makes high-performance carbon fiber under the Tenax brand. Tenax intermediate-modulus fiber (e.g. IMS65) is qualified into aerospace structural use (NCAMP qualification with Syensqo resin; separately qualified by Collins Aerospace). Part of the merchant aerospace carbon-fiber material tier feeding launch-vehicle composite structures.
nodes.notes: Tenax carbon fiber; aerospace-qualified (NCAMP with Syensqo Prism EP2400; Collins Aerospace). Ticker 3401.T (Tokyo) verified this round. No launch-program-specific share found; mapped as material-tier reported_capable_supplier.

nodes.name: Mitsubishi Chemical Group
nodes.description: Japanese chemicals group (Tokyo: 4188); makes Pyrofil PAN carbon fiber and Newport composites used in aircraft systems and structural parts as well as missiles, rockets and satellites. Has Pyrofil intermediate-modulus aerospace grades and is doubling carbon-fiber capacity at Tokai (Japan) and Sacramento (US) over 2025-2027 for high-end applications including aerospace. Part of the merchant aerospace carbon-fiber material tier.
nodes.notes: Pyrofil carbon fiber used in aircraft/missile/rocket/satellite structures; capacity doubling 2025-2027 (Tokai + Sacramento). Ticker 4188.T (Tokyo) verified this round — NOTE distinct from existing org_mitsubishi_gas_chemical and org_mitsubishi_electric. No launch-program-specific share; material-tier reported_capable_supplier.

nodes.name: Syensqo
nodes.description: Specialty-materials company (Euronext Brussels: SYENS) carved out of Solvay in December 2023; holds the legacy Solvay/Cytec composite-materials business. Supplies aerospace-qualified epoxy resin systems and prepregs (e.g. Prism EP2400, NCAMP-qualified with Teijin Tenax fiber) plus carbon fiber for aerospace structures. Represents the resin/prepreg (matrix) half of the merchant carbon-composite material tier that feeds launch-vehicle composite structures.
nodes.notes: Holds legacy Solvay/Cytec composites business post Dec-2023 spin-off; aerospace-qualified resin/prepreg (Prism EP2400, NCAMP). Listed Euronext Brussels SYENS (ISIN BE0003851681) — verified this round; do NOT attribute to legacy Solvay ticker. Resin/matrix-tier reported_capable_supplier.

nodes.name: Infinite Composites
nodes.description: U.S. (Tulsa, OK) maker of linerless (Type V) composite pressure vessels and COPVs for pressurant and propellant tanks in launch vehicles, satellites, lunar landers and space fueling depots. Private company; government/research customers shown include NASA, U.S. Air Force, U.S. Army. Represents the merchant COPV population that non-captive launch programs can buy (SpaceX itself builds COPVs in-house).
nodes.notes: Private; merchant COPV / linerless CPV maker for launch vehicles & spacecraft. No verified ticker (private) — not guessed. reported_capable_supplier to the COPV component (SpaceX COPV is captive).

nodes.name: Steelhead Composites
nodes.description: U.S. (Golden, CO) maker of high-performance COPVs integrated into launch-vehicle propulsion systems and used as primary/auxiliary tanks for spacecraft propulsion, with liners selected for hypergolic, cryogenic or pressurized-gas propellant compatibility. Private company; part of the merchant COPV population for the broader launch/space industry.
nodes.notes: Private; merchant COPV maker for launch-vehicle propulsion & spacecraft. No verified ticker (private) — not guessed. reported_capable_supplier to the COPV component.

nodes.name: HyPerComp Engineering
nodes.description: U.S. (Brigham City, UT) developer, qualifier and producer of composite-overwrapped pressure vessels (COPVs); AS9100-D, products used in space launch vehicles among other applications. Co-developed a Type IV carbon-overwrap COPV with Hexcel using HexTow IM11-R/12K carbon fiber for aerospace and space. Private company; part of the merchant COPV population.
nodes.notes: Private (founded 1996, <20 employees, AS9100-D); merchant COPV maker for space launch vehicles. No verified ticker (private). reported_capable_supplier; also links the carbon-fiber tier (Hexcel HexTow IM11-R) into COPV overwrap.

nodes.name: General Dynamics Ordnance and Tactical Systems
nodes.description: Composite-structures unit (Lincoln Operations) of General Dynamics (NYSE: GD). Design authority for the NASA SLS Core Stage and Upper Stage COPVs and for multiple satellite COPVs that provide compressed gas for propulsion subsystems; applications also include launch-vehicle and satellite propulsion. Listed via parent General Dynamics. Part of the merchant COPV population (SLS, satellites — not SpaceX, which is captive).
nodes.notes: GD-OTS Lincoln Operations; design authority for SLS Core/Upper Stage COPVs and satellite COPVs. Listed via parent General Dynamics (NYSE: GD) — subsidiary; ticker is the parent's, verified this round. reported_capable_supplier to the COPV component.

edges.claim: Falcon 9 payload fairings (and other launch-vehicle composite structures) are built from aerospace carbon-fiber composite; the fiber+resin material is the merchant tier while fairing lay-up/cure is captive at SpaceX.

COPVs storing high-pressure helium sit inside the propellant tankage and pressurize the tanks as propellant is consumed; the pressurant-vessel sub-component hangs off the tank/airframe structure module.
COPV overwrap is aerospace carbon-fiber composite over a metal/polymer liner, tying the pressurant vessel back to the same merchant carbon-fiber material tier.
Toray is the world's largest carbon fiber producer and supplies aerospace-grade intermediate-/high-modulus fiber used in aircraft primary structure and the launch-vehicle composite material tier.
Hexcel HexTow carbon fiber and HexPly prepreg are preferred aerospace primary-structure materials (787, A350 XWB, JSF); a merchant carbon-fiber + prepreg supplier in this tier.
Teijin Carbon's Tenax intermediate-modulus carbon fiber is aerospace-qualified (NCAMP with Syensqo resin; Collins Aerospace) — a merchant supplier in the aerospace carbon-fiber tier.

Mitsubishi Chemical Pyrofil PAN carbon fiber and Newport composites are used in aircraft, missile, rocket and satellite structural parts — a merchant supplier in the aerospace carbon-fiber tier, expanding capacity 2025-2027.

Syensqo (legacy Solvay/Cytec composites) supplies aerospace-qualified epoxy resin systems and prepregs (Prism EP2400, NCAMP-qualified) plus carbon fiber — the resin/matrix half of the merchant carbon-composite material tier.
SpaceX builds its own COPVs in-house (captive) for Falcon 9 helium pressurant storage.
Infinite Composites makes COPVs / linerless CPVs for pressurant and propellant tanks in launch vehicles and spacecraft — merchant supplier to the wider industry (SpaceX COPV is captive).
Steelhead Composites makes COPVs integrated into launch-vehicle propulsion systems and spacecraft propulsion tanks — merchant supplier to the wider industry.
HyPerComp Engineering develops/qualifies/produces COPVs used in space launch vehicles; Type IV COPV co-developed with Hexcel HexTow IM11-R fiber — merchant supplier to the wider industry.
GD-OTS Lincoln Operations is design authority for NASA SLS Core/Upper Stage COPVs and satellite propulsion COPVs — merchant supplier to the wider launch/space industry (not SpaceX, which is captive).
